name: Dowsing Dagger // Lost Vale

abilities.text: When ~ enters, target opponent creates two 0/2 green Plant creature tokens with defender.
Whenever equipped creature deals combat damage to a player, you may transform ~.
{T}: Add three mana of any one color.

notes: Front: the ETB gives the opponent two Plant walls; the flip trigger uses filter attachedToSource (CR 702.6a) so it fires only on the equipped creature's combat damage to a player, and 'you may transform' is a may around the transform op. 'Equip {2}' is claimed by its own activated ability (attach-self) because the format has no covers kind for equip. Back: Lost Vale's three mana of one colour is add-mana 'any-one' with amount 3.

abilities.how: static: the board differs with and without this ability

issues: Whenever equipped creature deals combat damage to a player, you may transform this Equipment. — expected fires whenever the creature this Equipment is attached to deals combat damage to a player, regardless of who controls that creature (CR 702.6a: "equipped creature" is defined by the attachment, not by control) — scripted event combat-damage-player + filter.attachedToSource is the right expression, but game.ts:2271 gates the filter branch on `ctx.obj.controller === perm.controller` as well, so a creature whose control an opponent gained while the Dagger stayed attached would not trigger. Engine-side restriction, not a mis-expression; noted, not verdict-flipping. — CR 702.6a / 301.5c

When this Equipment enters, target opponent creates two 0/2 green Plant creature tokens with defender. — expected the tokens are created (and controlled/owned) by the targeted opponent; each token is named "Plant" — scripted scoped who=target-opponent + token is correct — legal.ts:84 derives the {kind:'opponent'} target requirement from the scoped who, and game.ts:1062 makes the token op use item.actor as controller/owner. Only gap: token.name is left undefined, so the engine calls it "Plant token" (game.ts:1379) rather than "Plant". Corpus-wide convention (parse.ts:747 does the same), so not scored against this script. The renderer's 0.86 line is a render gap only — it drops "target opponent". — CR 111.4

// {T}: Add three mana of any one color. — expected three mana all of the SAME chosen color — scripted add-mana mana:'any-one', amount:3 — mana.ts:54-56 pushes one option per color of Array(3).fill(c), i.e. three of one color. Correct despite the renderer printing the awkward "add 3 one mana of any color". — CR 106.1b
